newsitem.title: UK: FORECAST-Smith & Nephew set for higher profit.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Smith & Nephew set for higher profit.

text.p: Healthcare group Smith & Nephew Plc is set to announce solid profit growth on Tuesday when the group announces its full-year results, analysts said.
They expect few surprises after a meeting with the company early in January, which left them assured Smith & Nephew is coping well with tough market conditions and the impact of a strong pound.
Analysts expect pre-tax profit to come in between 182 and 197 million stg amid signs that profit margins were better in the second half of the year than in the first.
Smith & Nephew posted a pre-tax profit of 180.4 million in 1995.

The company signalled in January that sales in the highly competitive U.S. market had risen two percent in the second half of 1996 after a gain of just 0.5 percent in the in the first six months of the year.

Prices in the U.S., which accounts for around 40 percent of Smith & Nephew's turnover, are under pressure in such areas as orthopaedic implants and wound management by increasingly powerful health providers.

Analysts said they will be looking for comments from Smith & Nephew on its novel skin replacement product Dermagraft. But most expect it will take at least another month before it is possible to get a clear picture of the product's fortunes.
High hopes for Dermagraft sales sent Smith & Nephew shares soaring in the middle of last year. They got a boost again earlier this month as smouldering take-over rumours flared up.
But industry watchers take them with a pinch of salt.
"They are as old as the arc," said an analyst.
